subject: [Incident] Parquet Labs - Dedicated GPU pool degradation (initial notice)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: ops@parquetlabs.com, engineering@parquetlabs.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0500
Subject: [Incident] Parquet Labs - Dedicated GPU pool degradation (initial notice)

Hi Alex / Parquet team,

We wanted to notify you proactively that our Dedicated GPU pool serving your account experienced a degradation event beginning ~2027-11-20 09:48 UTC that impacted tail latency and request throughput for a subset of your routes. Our operations team detected increased queueing on the warmup allocator which produced sustained 95th/99th percentile latency elevations for ~45 minutes.

Immediate status: we applied a temporary routing bridge to move traffic to warm spare capacity and disabled aggressive prefetching for the affected node set. This reduced error rates and brought tail latencies back to acceptable thresholds.

Observed impact:
- Elevated 95/99 P50 token latency for generation routes (up to 3.4x baseline)
- Intermittent 503s for long-context streaming requests (estimated 0.7% of your requests during the window)
- No data exposure; this was a performance degradation only

Next steps we are executing now:
1) Collecting full allocator and kernel telemetry and will upload an evidence bundle (ETA 2 hours).
2) Performing controlled remediation to remove a memory-pressure-inducing prefetch path (Ben is leading).
3) Preparing a post-incident summary and credit proposal if our SLA thresholds were missed.

Ben and Marissa are on the thread for technical follow-up and remediation coordination. I will update you within 3 hours with the evidence link and interim ETA for the full postmortem.

We appreciate your patience — apologies for the disruption. If you prefer a brief run-through with our SREs right now, we can jump on a call.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

Alex — quick technical update and artifacts.

TL;DR: Root cause is a warmup allocator loop triggered by an aggressive model prefetch path under specific sequence-length distribution; this caused uneven KV cache growth and eviction storms on 3 nodes in your tenant's subpool. We applied a conservative patch to disable that prefetch path and drained the affected nodes.

What we collected and attached:
- redwood_evidence_parquet_20271120.tar.gz (allocator traces, kernel logs, kv-cache metrics, node heartbeats)
- roadmap_parquet_prefetch_mitigation.md (short explanation of the conservative change applied)

Key timeline (UTC):
- 09:48:02 — allocator queue depth rises on nodes a03,a07,a09
- 09:50:20 — tail latency spikes; 503s observed for long-streaming sessions
- 09:57:40 — automated warm-spare bridge engaged (traffic redirection)
- 10:02:13 — prefetch path disabled on affected nodes (mitigation applied)
- 10:12:55 — observed tail latency returned to baseline; error rate normalized by 10:30

Mitigations performed:
1) Traffic bridging to warm spare capacity (reduced client disruption)
2) Stateful drain and patch of three nodes to clear KV evictions
3) Throttled prefetch and lowered prewarm concurrency for your subpool as an immediate protective measure

Short-term actions we recommend for Parquet (optional):
- If you prefer, we can configure an automated model-variant fallback for long-stream clients (we can do this for an agreed maintenance window).
- Reduce max-prefetch in your client config by 20% for the next 48 hours; we'll monitor and revert if safe.

Evidence link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-evidence/parquet/2027-11-20/redwood_evidence_parquet_20271120.tar.gz
Jira: https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/RDW-4312

Attachment stub: [Attachment: redwood_evidence_parquet_20271120.tar.gz (120MB)]

We'll produce a full postmortem within 72 hours with root cause analysis, longer-term mitigations (kernel and autoscaler changes), and a credit proposal if SLA thresholds were missed. Marissa will coordinate postmortem scheduling.

- Ben

Hi Alex, team — closing note and next steps from the customer ops / account side.

Thanks again for the quick coordination last weekend. We completed the detailed postmortem and remediation plan; highlights below and attached:

Summary: A prefetch-induced eviction storm in a subset of your dedicated nodes produced transient resource starvation. The protective bridge limited request loss; however, your SLA windows for 99th percentile token latency were impacted between 09:50–10:12 UTC.

Remediations and long-term fixes we will deliver in upcoming releases:
- Autoscaler: improvements to allocation smoothing to avoid local node oscillation (RDW-4312).
- Runtime: guardrails to detect KV growth runaway and apply local prefetch backoff without global draining.
- Rollout: a conservative prefetch profile will be the default for tenants on high-rise sequence distributions; we will provide a toggle for advanced customers.

Compensation: We ran the SLA math and will issue a service credit equivalent to 6% of your November usage bill for the affected routes. Formal credit documentation will follow by invoice update next week.

Attachments: parquet_playbook_patch.diff (patch summary), redwood_evidence_parquet_20271120.tar.gz (allocator logs)
Timeline for the postmortem report: Final postmortem published to the Drive link and Jira ticket (RDW-4312) by 2027-11-27 18:00 UTC.

If you'd like a short walkthrough with engineering, Ben is available Thursday 16:00 UTC. Let us know if that works and whether you prefer a focused deep-dive or an executive summary.

Apologies for the disruption, and thank you for your partnership.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
